transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-04 09:00 PT
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Locale: US
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Granite Pulse Head of Security), Alex Ruiz (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood walked Granite Pulse through SAML provisioning options (IdP metadata, assertion attributes), SCIM group/user sync mapping and deprovision flows, RBAC role hierarchy and least-privilege model, and KMS integration patterns (BYOK, envelope encryption, HSM). Discussed audit logging, retention, SIEM forward, and data residency controls. Next step: share SOC2/ISO docs, SCIM mapping template, and schedule KMS POC.

Topics: SAML SSO setup; SCIM attribute mapping; Just-in-time vs SCIM bulk provisioning; role boundaries and least privilege; KMS/BYOK and HSM; audit logs & SIEM; data residency; Dedicated vs Private deployment notes.

Action items (short): Jordan to send compliance docs; Priya to share mapping examples; Alex to give IdP metadata.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 45, 50 minutes blocked — we'll try to keep tight. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya (Granite Pulse): Maya here, Head of Security. we run the platform team oversight for identity and compliance.
[00:12] Alex (Granite Pulse): Alex, platform eng, I'll own the integration and testing.
[00:15] Samir (Granite Pulse): Samir, compliance, mostly here to confirm controls map back to SOC2 and ISO questions.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Priya's our SE and she'll go deep on the SAML/SCIM + KMS patterns. Priya, over to you?
[00:26] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick agenda: SAML SSO flow and required attributes, SCIM provisioning and group-to-role mapping, RBAC examples for least-privilege, and key management options — BYOK, Redwood-managed KMS, HSM integrations. Also we'll cover audit log retention and SIEM forwarding.
[00:40] Maya: Cool. For context, we're a regulated payments company — data residency is strict, logs must stay in EU for EU customers, and we have a SOC2 Type II due soon so we need artifacts. We also prefer IdP-first provisioning but may accept SCIM sync.
[00:58] Jordan: Understood. Quick qual — do you currently use an IdP?
[01:02] Maya: Yes, we use Okta as our primary IdP, SCIM is enabled for some apps, group sync is in place. We also have some service accounts in AWS KMS and rotate keys quarterly.
[01:16] Priya: Okta is familiar — our SAML flows have been tested with Okta a lot. Two provisioning patterns to consider: JIT (just-in-time) SAML provisioning which creates accounts on first login using assertion attributes, or SCIM push provisioning which maintains user/group state from IdP to Redwood. Both have tradeoffs.
[01:35] Alex: We prefer deterministic deprovisioning — SCIM is safer there. JIT leaves orphan accounts if group membership changes.
[01:42] Priya: Totally. For deprovisioning we recommend SCIM for employee lifecycle. We support SCIM 2.0 — common pitfalls are attribute mapping and unique id selection (e.g., use immutable employee id as externalId).
[01:56] Samir: On mapping, we need to ensure roles are mapped to groups and there's no privilege creep.
[02:00] Priya: We'll show an example mapping where SCIM groups map to Redwood roles: e.g., scim group 'gp_admins' -> Redwood role 'org-admin' (limited to RBAC admin actions, not key management). Quick note — we separate RBAC roles for app-level access vs infra-level ops (like key rotation).
[02:22] Jordan: Also to call out — in Dedicated and Private deployments the customer can use their own KMS; in hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK as an option. Priya, can you explain the BYOK flow?
[02:34] Priya: Sure. There are two typical patterns: 1) Customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) integrated so Redwood never has plaintext root keys — we use envelope encryption with a data key wrapped by the customer's KMS CMK. 2) HSM-backed keys for FIPS/HSM compliance where you rotate in hardware. For both we keep minimal plaintext in memory; the runtime gets ephemeral data keys and caches decrypted KV in process but not persisted. Note: some transcriptions might say K-V cash or KV cache, but that's our in-memory token cache.
[03:05] Maya: So Redwood never stores the unwrapped customer master key?
[03:08] Priya: Correct. We only store wrapped keys; the CMK stays in your KMS/HSM. You can revoke or rotate and we will failover to fallback keys per policy.
[03:20] Alex: How do we handle key rotation and token revocation with active sessions? We can't drop all in-flight requests.
[03:26] Priya: We have a rotation window — rotations apply to new envelopes, existing data keys remain valid until rewrap is completed. For sessions we support graceful rekeying and a TTL for caches. Our runtime evicts stale KV cache entries on rekey. There's an SLO tradeoff — you get slightly increased latency during rewrap windows but not full cutoff.
[03:47] Samir: Do you provide attestation or HSM audit trails? We need evidence for the audit.
[03:52] Jordan: We can share KMS integration docs and HSM attestation templates. For enterprise customers on Private, we can arrange direct HSM connectors and provide logs.
[04:03] Maya: Ok. On audit logs, we need logs forwarded to our SIEM, with immutable storage and a tamper-evident trail. Retention for six years for some records. Can Redwood support that?
[04:15] Priya: Yes — audit logs include request metadata, token IDs, model and route, user/account id, and decision events (e.g., policy fallback). We support log streaming to S3 (in-region) or to an HTTPS SIEM endpoint via secure delivery. Retention policies can be controlled on your sink. For tamper-evidence we sign logs and publish hash digests to an external ledger if needed.
[04:37] Alex: Will logs for EU customers remain in EU?
[04:39] Jordan: For Private deployments we can host in your VPC/region. For Hosted we offer region-aware log sinks and can configure EU-only storage. We'll need to add data residency clauses to the contract.
[04:51] Maya: Good. Next, SCIM attribute details — what attributes are required in SAML assertion and SCIM payload for correct mapping?
[04:58] Priya: For SAML JIT we rely on attributes: email, firstName, lastName, and optionally groups. For SCIM we expect id/externalId, userName (email), displayName, active boolean, and group members arrays. Important: pick a stable externalId (employee id) as the canonical key — email can change.
[05:20] Alex: We have a custom attribute 'gp_employee_id' we can map.
[05:23] Priya: Perfect — that'll be the externalId. Also, group membership sync frequency matters. Okta can do immediate push or scheduled; we recommend near-real-time for high-churn teams.
[05:37] Jordan: On RBAC — we typically recommend a small set of roles with least privilege and use group-based role assignment. Priya, example?
[05:44] Priya: Example baseline roles: viewer (read-only, no cost-affecting actions), editor (could create prompts and call models but not change infra), admin (manage org settings and users), security-audit (view audit & logs only), keys-ops (rotate keys, access to KMS settings) — note keys-ops is separated and requires an extra approval workflow. We advise role separation of duties for compliance.
[06:10] Samir: Good, separation of duties is necessary. How granular are the Redwood audit events — can we filter by API key, route, or token owner?
[06:19] Priya: Yes — events include api_key_id, token_owner, route, model, response size, latency, and decision flags. You can filter and ingest to SIEM.
[06:28] Maya: On admin ops — can we enforce MFA and conditional access for Redwood console admins?
[06:32] Jordan: Yes. We support SSO with conditional access policies via IdP. For console-level MFA you can require step-up through IdP rules.
[06:40] Alex: What about service accounts and machine-to-machine auth? We want short-lived tokens and rotation.
[06:45] Priya: We recommend short-lived JWT tokens minted with OIDC flows + rotating private keys. For Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your internal STS. We also expose token rotation APIs and recommend automatic rotation every X hours.
[06:58] Maya: Questions on SCIM: how are group-to-role mappings edited? Does Redwood have a UI and an API?
[07:04] Priya: Both. There's a Console UI for mapping and an API for programmatic updates. The mapping can be one-to-one or many-to-many (e.g., multiple groups map to a single role). We store mapping as simple rules and we surface an audit trail for any mapping changes.
[07:19] Alex: If a user is in multiple groups with conflicting roles, what wins?
[07:22] Priya: We evaluate highest-permission wins by default, but you can change precedence rules (deny overrides highest-perm) based on your org policy. We can recommend deny-overrides for strict environments.
[07:35] Jordan: Let's touch on provisioning scale — do you expect tens of thousands of users or just hundreds?
[07:40] Maya: Initially a few hundred, but scale could grow to 10k across global regions in two years.
[07:46] Priya: We handle large SCIM deltas; best practice is to do initial bulk sync and then incremental deltas. Also note rate limits — we'll share recommended bulk window settings and throttles.
[07:58] Samir: From a compliance standpoint we need role-change approvals recorded. Does Redwood capture requested role changes and approver identity?
[08:05] Priya: Yes — we capture change request metadata and approver identities if the change is done via the Console. For API-driven changes you can send approval metadata and we persist it as part of the audit event.
[08:16] Alex: KMS POC — we want to test envelope encryption with our AWS KMS CMK, can Redwood load test that path?
[08:22] Jordan: Absolutely. Typical POC steps: share IdP metadata + test users, provide KMS test CMK ARN and permissions, create small benchmark of token issuance and request patterns, and validate logs in your SIEM.
[08:34] Priya: For the POC we'll spin up a sandbox with your CMK bound and show rekey rotation flows. Note that in hosted mode we may route through a regional proxy for EU keys; in Private you can keep keys in your VPC.
[08:48] Maya: One concern: emergency key revocation — we need a documented process and SLA for key rotation or emergency revocation.
[08:55] Jordan: We have runbooks for emergency key revocation and a switch-over plan. We'll share the runbook; for Private customers we can do on-call support.
[09:03] Samir: Regarding SOC2 mapping — can you provide control IDs mapped to your features (e.g., how RBAC maps to CC6.1 etc.)?
[09:11] Jordan: Yes, Jordan: we'll provide a control-mapping spreadsheet that ties specific Redwood features and docs to SOC2 control criteria and ISO clauses.
[09:19] Priya: One nit — some customers want to mask PII in logs. We offer redaction rules and PII scrubbing for request/response bodies before they hit long-term storage.
[09:31] Alex: Good. How about export encryption for backups?
[09:34] Priya: Backups are encrypted in transit and at rest. If you use BYOK we wrap backups with your CMK. For extra assurance we can provide proof of encryption via key usage logs.
[09:45] Maya: Any limitations around SCIM with nested groups or large group membership?
[09:50] Priya: SCIM spec doesn't enforce nested groups widely; our SCIM supports groups with member arrays. For nested groups we recommend flattening in IdP or doing mapping rules. For very large groups we support pagination and chunked sync.
[10:04] Jordan: I'm going to summarise next steps — Jordan to send compliance/docs, Priya to send SCIM template & RBAC starter matrix, and Alex to provide IdP metadata. Any blockers?
[10:15] Maya: None on our side. Timeline — we want SOC2 evidence and RBAC mapping within two weeks.
[10:20] Samir: We'll also want legal to review BYOK contract language — can you share standard clauses?
[10:25] Jordan: Yes, we'll send standard BYOK and data residency contract language.
[10:28] Alex: For the POC, estimated time to stand up sandbox? 1-2 weeks after metadata and CMK access?
[10:33] Priya: That matches our typical timeline. We'll need a small test user set and permissions on the CMK (GenerateDataKey and Encrypt/Decrypt for the Redwood service principal).
[10:45] Maya: Are there any known compliance gaps we should be aware of?
[10:49] Priya: Nothing major — most gaps are around customer-specific policies (e.g., longer retention, different approver flows). We can accommodate via configuration and runbooks.
[10:58] Jordan: Ok great. Anything else?
[11:00] Samir: Just confirm we get a copy of the HSM attestation if we go that route.
[11:03] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide attestation artifacts where applicable.
[11:06] Priya: I'll compile a short tech checklist for the POC: IdP metadata, SCIM endpoints & credentials, CMK ARN + test permissions, test users CSV, SIEM endpoint for log streaming.
[11:18] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[11:22] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the POC.

End summary (auto):
- Agreed: SCIM preferred for deprovisioning; mapping by externalId; group->role mapping by rules.
